policies.title: Mongolia: residual ordinary passports require an advance tourist visa
policies.summary: Mongolia's Foreign Ministry directs foreign nationals outside its named eVisa cohort to apply at the nearest Mongolian embassy. These 24 ordinary passports are also outside the current ordinary-passport exemption and border-tourist cohorts, so their unconditional short-visitor route requires advance mission issuance.
conditions: Applies to standard ordinary passports used for a short tourist visit; work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service and other special-document routes remain outside scope.
Cuba, Azerbaijan, North Korea and Turkmenistan have special-passport exemptions in the current schedule, but those agreements do not exempt the standard ordinary passports classified here.

The applicant submits the visa application and printed supporting documents at a Mongolian diplomatic mission. The normal stated processing time is three working days, but some applications may take five to ten working days.
A regular tourist visa normally permits up to 30 days. The passport must be valid for at least six months, additional evidence may be requested and final admission remains discretionary.

policies.title: Indian ordinary passports: visa-free Honduras visitor entry
policies.summary: The current CA-4 schedule directly places Indian ordinary passports in Category A, defined as visa-exempt, and expressly applies that schedule to Honduras. Honduras's Immigration Institute directs tourist visitors to the CA-4 category system.
conditions: Applies to a valid Indian ordinary passport used for a short tourist visit; diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit and other special-document rules remain outside scope.
The passport should remain valid for at least six months. Purpose, funds, onward travel, health and individual-admissibility requirements continue to apply.
A tourist may normally remain for up to 90 days and may seek a further 30-day extension from Honduras's Immigration Institute.
The current CA-4 schedule became effective on 16 April 2026; later national deviations or replacement schedules require recheck.

conflicts.explanation: Mongolia's exemption schedule limits Cuba's agreement to diplomatic and official passports. A standard Cuban ordinary passport is outside the current eVisa and border-tourist cohorts and follows the express embassy-application residual.
The current CA-4 table directly marks India's ordinary passport Category A, visa-exempt, and states that the schedule determines the visa type for Honduras.
